chapterNote: The household psalm — a Song of Ascents that the church has read at weddings for centuries — it stands in the Eastern crowning rite and in the old English marriage service --, because it is the shortest complete picture of a blessed home in the Bible. It starts with the one condition — everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in His ways — and then shows what that fear produces at the dinner table: you will eat what your own hands have worked for, and it will go well with you; your wife like a fruitful vine in the inner rooms of the house; your children like olive shoots around the table — young trees that will outlast you. Look, says the psalm, THIS is how the man is blessed who fears the LORD. Then the blessing widens, as the Ascents so often do, from the household to the city and the nation: may the LORD bless you from Zion; may you see Jerusalem's good all your days; may you see your children's children — and peace upon Israel. A God-fearing family is the first school of the kingdom of God, and this psalm is its portrait.

1.text: A song of ascents. Oh the blessedness of everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in His ways!
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth]. Blessed [esher] is every one that fears [yare] the LORD [YHWH]; that walks [halak] in His ways [derek].
1.notes: ashre kol-yere YHWH (H835, H3373, H3068): the beatitude, for EVERY God-fearer — ha-holekh bi-derakhav (H1980, H1870): the one walking in His roads. Fear and walking: the inner posture and the outer route, Psalm 1's blessed man on the pilgrim road.

2.text: You will surely eat the fruit of your hands' labor; happy will you be, and it will go well with you.
2.amp: For you shall eat [akal] the labour [yegia — toil, the fruit of toil] of your hands [kaph]: happy [esher] shall you be, and it shall be well [tov] with you.
2.notes: yegia kappekha ki tokhel (H3018, H3709, H398): you will EAT your palms' toil — the curse of Genesis 3 turned right side up: work that feeds the worker, not a stranger (cf. Deuteronomy 28:33 for the reverse) — ashrekha ve-tov lakh (H835, H2896): happy you, and good to you. Blessedness measured in an honest supper.

3.text: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine in the inner rooms of your house; your children like olive shoots all around your table.
3.amp: Your wife [ishshah] shall be as a fruitful [parah] vine [gephen] by the sides [yerekah — the inner recesses] of your house [bayith]: your children [ben] like olive [zayith] plants [shathil — shoots, transplants] round about [sabib] your table [shulchan].
3.notes: eshtekha ke-gephen poriyyah be-yarkete betekha (H802, H1612, H6509, H3411, H1004): the wife a fruitful vine in the house's inner recesses — the private rooms, where the family actually lives — banekha ki-shtile zetim sabib le-shulchanekha (H1121, H8363, H2132, H5439, H7979): the children olive SHOOTS around the table: the young trees that spring up around an old olive's base and will bear for a century after the parent is gone. The vine and the olive, staples of Israel's table with grain (Deuteronomy 8:8), the olive among the longest-lived things in the land, seated at one table.

4.text: Look: this is how the man who fears the LORD is blessed!
4.amp: Behold, that thus shall the man [geber] be blessed [barak] that fears [yare] the LORD [YHWH].
4.notes: hinneh khi-khen yeborakh geber yere YHWH (H1288, H1397, H3373, H3068): LOOK — like THIS — the geber, the strong man, is blessed: not with conquest but with a table. The psalm points at verse 3 and says: that is the blessing.

5.text: May the LORD bless you from Zion; may you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life,
5.amp: The LORD [YHWH] shall bless [barak] you out of Zion [Tsiyyon]: and you shall see [raah] the good [tuv] of Jerusalem [Yerushalaim] all the days [yom] of your life [chay].
5.notes: yebarekhkha YHWH mi-Tsiyyon (H1288, H3068, H6726): the blessing's source is the sanctuary, Psalm 134:3's formula — u-reeh be-tuv Yerushalaim kol yeme chayyekha (H7200, H2898, H3389, H3117, H2416): may you look on Jerusalem's good every day you live. The household is blessed from the city; the Ascents never let the family forget the temple.

6.text: and may you live to see your children's children. Peace upon Israel!
6.amp: Yea, you shall see [raah] your children's [ben] children, and peace [shalom] upon Israel [Yisrael].
6.notes: u-reeh-banim le-banekha (H7200, H1121): see sons to your sons — grandchildren, the olive shoots' shoots — shalom al-Yisrael (H7965, H3478): Psalm 125:5's benediction. Table, city, nation, generations: the blessing radiates outward from one God-fearing man's dinner.
